claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed jointly by a composition-dependent thermodynamic driving force and temperature-dependent atomic diffusion.
A slight increase in Al content amplifies thermodynamic instability in this alloy.
The Al-amplified instability favors chemical ordering.
The Al-amplified instability favors phase separation.
High-temperature diffusion in the BCC state enables short-range ordered clusters to evolve.
Short-range ordered clusters act as precursors to a structural transformation.
The initial Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 alloy is a homogeneous high-temperature BCC phase.
The initial alloy has a uniform elemental distribution.
Temperature-dependent phase fractions and diffraction peak shifts or splittings reflect the emergence of short-range ordering.
The diffraction changes reflect nucleation and growth of secondary ordered phases.
Increasing local Al content decreases the thermochemical stability of the BCC phase by increasing the driving force for ordering.
High-temperature atomic mobility facilitates the diffusion-controlled transition.
Transformation onset is advanced in Al-enriched regions because enhanced thermodynamic instability is paired with rapid atomic rearrangement.
The Al-modified samples will begin ordering earlier than the baseline sample.
Earlier ordering will be observable through diffraction peak splitting and shifts associated with secondary-phase formation.
If XRD does not resolve subtle ordering, TEM or atom-probe tomography should reveal short-range ordered clusters.
The proposed mechanism may not apply below 1100 degrees Celsius or to substantially different compositions.
No measurable composition-dependent difference in ordering onset or phase-fraction evolution would falsify the proposed Al-dependent mechanism.

contradictions.description: The comparison includes both +1 at.% and -1 at.% Al variants, but the predicted outcome says the 'Al-modified samples' will both order earlier, whereas the mechanism specifically predicts earlier onset only for Al enrichment. The expected direction for the Al-depleted variant is not stated consistently.

The conditions state that samples are heated from the high-temperature BCC state, while the falsification design states that they cool from 1350°C to 1100°C. The thermal path is therefore described inconsistently.
